description: The Format-2 in-place table SORT - a COBOL-2002 introduction, recognized syntactically (a SORT with neither USING/GIVING nor INPUT/OUTPUT procedures is the F2 shape). Folded from the inline SortBinder gate (Exec Step E). THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): the 1985 SORT sorts a sort file only ('The SORT statement creates a sort file by executing an input procedure or by transferring records from another file', §1985:XI.4.4.1; §1985:XI.4.4.3 SR2: 'File-name-1 must be described in a sort-merge file description entry in the Data Division'); §2002:14.8.36 reads 'The SORT statement causes a set of records or table elements to be arranged in a user-specified sequence', its Format 2 (table) sorting data-name-2 (§2002:14.8.36.2 SR13: 'Data-name-2 may be qualified and shall have an OCCURS clause in its data description entry'), and §2002:F.2 states the change, its item 125: 'A SORT statement may be used to sort a table.' §2014:14.9.36 and §2014:14.9.36.2 SR13 carry it, so 2014 = 2023.
